status: What the ontology lacks to answer evals/dev/amazon-fba/proposed_items.json: one entry per ranked gap (map_rank 1-7), weak link or dependency of the Amazon FBA Replenishment Map, plus the unread originals. map_says is the map's claim, attributed to Greg's walkthrough of 16 Oct 2026; implementation, where present, is a claim about deployed code that nobody here verified (the map's author read no Portal or BC code). Sources are named, never read here; OntologyProject refs are at the base f635203cfe41, the map's record at codex/advisory e58e8a98f3ef. 'source unknown' carries the question for Greg or Vince that would find one.

gaps.map_gap: Create a shipment order for Amazon replenishment
gaps.name: ReplenishmentShipment (one Amazon inbound shipment of PLX stock: Amazon shipment ID, FC, status, OR, BOL, freight booking, lines in cases)
gaps.map_says: nothing holds one Amazon replenishment shipment from stock check to tracking; the Sage OR is raised before Amazon assigns the FC and is then revised
gaps.implementation: the map labels the Portal shipment order 'not built'; unverified against Portal code
gaps.ontology_today: SalesOrder (sage.oe_order_header) and Shipment (Sage OE, Portal and BC bindings) exist; neither carries an Amazon shipment ID or an Amazon FC, and Shipment.same_record_as needs a stable shared key the map says does not exist.

gaps.map_gap: Connect Seller Central inbound (Amazon shipment ID, FC, labels)
gaps.name: Shipment.amazon_inbound_shipment (an OR or shipment to the Amazon shipment ID it fulfils; one order per Amazon shipment)
gaps.map_says: the Amazon shipment ID is on none of the OR, packing slip or BOL; it is the only key that joins Amazon, Sage, Freightcom and BC
gaps.implementation: the map reports a dashboard SP-API connection whose inbound/fulfilment role is unverified
gaps.ontology_today: No Amazon or SP-API object, binding or source registry entry exists.

sources.relation: the map's advisory record (the claim, not a reader)

gaps.dot_question: Greg or Vince: does PLX's Seller Central app (the dashboard's SP-API connection) hold the inbound/fulfilment role, and may a read-only reader use it to list inbound shipments with their shipment ID, FC and box/pallet labels?

gaps.map_gap: Amazon inventory feed and low-stock alert (45/90 days on last-30-day sales)
gaps.name: Amazon FBA on-hand, inbound and last-30-day sales per seller SKU, with as-of date
gaps.map_says: the trigger is a manual Seller Central check with no threshold; the rule Greg stated is alert below 45 days of supply, replenish to 90, on last-30-day sales, for every brand
gaps.implementation: the map says nothing in the Portal watches Amazon inventory; unverified against Portal code
gaps.ontology_today: No object or reader for Amazon inventory or sales; no days-of-supply measure.
gaps.dot_question: Greg or Vince: which system is the source of truth for last-30-day Amazon sales per SKU (Seller Central reports, the dashboard, Sage or another tool), and do days of supply count FBA inbound units?

gaps.map_gap: Warehouse screen for final dims, pallets and customs fields
gaps.name: ShipmentPallet (final pallet count, dimensions and weight, gross and net, captured before the freight quote)
gaps.map_says: final dims came by email after a quote was already put forward; net weight equals gross weight on the paperwork
gaps.implementation: the map labels the warehouse dims screen 'not built'; unverified
gaps.ontology_today: Shipment has no pallet, dimension or weight members the cards can cite.

sources.relation: the map's advisory record (the claim, not a reader)

gaps.dot_question: Greg or Vince: where are final pallet dims and weights recorded today (email only, Sage, the WMS) and who enters them?

gaps.map_gap: Generate customs documents from item data
gaps.name: CustomsDocument (commercial invoice and TSCA/USMCA certificates of one shipment: lines in units, certificate coverage per SKU, validity)
gaps.map_says: the customs invoice declares 144 units where 12 cases at case pack 8 are 96; the TSCA and USMCA certificates were reused from an earlier shipment and list other SKUs
gaps.ontology_today: No customs document or certificate object; Product has no certificate link.

sources.relation: the map's advisory record (the claim, not a reader)

gaps.dot_question: Greg or Vince: who prepares the customs packet and from which item data, and where are the signed certificates kept?

gaps.map_gap: Connect Freightcom (quote on final dims, booking, BOL, tracking)
gaps.name: Freightcom quote, booking, BOL, PRO/SCAC and tracking per shipment
gaps.map_says: freight is quoted and booked by hand in Freightcom; final freight is approved by the warehouse manager with Greg copied
gaps.implementation: the Portal source at the repo pin names Freightcom hosts in a WMS carrier config; whether that client quotes or books Amazon LTL is unverified
gaps.ontology_today: The source registry lists the Freightcom hosts as a Portal integration; no ontology object or Workbench reader covers a booking, BOL or tracking event.

sources.relation: Freightcom hosts in the WMS carrier config (implementation evidence only)
Freightcom hosts in the WMS carrier config (implementation evidence only)

gaps.dot_question: Greg or Vince: is the Portal's Freightcom client used for Amazon LTL quotes and bookings, and under which Freightcom account can a read-only reader list bookings, BOLs and tracking?

gaps.map_gap: Inventory move to an Amazon location in BC at BOL
gaps.name: Shipment.moved_by_transfer (the BOL of a replenishment shipment to the BC transfer posting that moves its stock to the Amazon location)
gaps.map_says: the move to VMI happens at BOL (Greg, confirmed 16 Oct 2026); in the real case stock already showed VMI before the BOL; BC has no Amazon location yet
gaps.implementation: a BC transfer order posted at BOL is the map's expectation of standard BC behaviour, not checked in the repo
gaps.ontology_today: ItemLedgerEntry is partial (entry types include transfer) and Warehouse is not served (it pends bc_warehouse.json); nothing links a shipment or BOL to a ledger entry by location.

gaps.map_gap: Case pack lives in people's heads
gaps.name: Product.case_pack (an item's units per case, cited to one ItemUnitOfMeasure row)
gaps.map_says: FNA305-2LP is 8 units per case (Greg, 16 Oct 2026) while the customs invoice implies 12
gaps.ontology_today: ItemUnitOfMeasure (sage.ic_item_uom) is the only source a unit conversion may cite; whether a case-pack row exists for each FBA SKU is unread.

gaps.map_gap: Item to Amazon SKU mapping unconfirmed
gaps.name: Product.amazon_listing (a PLX item to its Amazon seller SKU, FNSKU and ASIN)
gaps.map_says: unknown whether the Sage item number is the Amazon seller SKU; the map proposes storing seller SKU and FNSKU on the item
gaps.ontology_today: Product binds sage.ic_item; no Amazon listing identity exists.
gaps.dot_question: Greg or Vince: is the Sage item number used as the Amazon seller SKU, and where are FNSKU and ASIN kept per item?

gaps.map_gap: Warehouse stock accuracy (out of scope, assumed fixed separately)
gaps.name: On-hand per item and location with as-of time, and a shelf count to compare
gaps.map_says: for FNA305-500 the record showed 30 cases and 17 existed, found after the OR and the Amazon build
gaps.ontology_today: ItemLedgerEntry is partial; no cycle-count or shelf-count object.

gaps.map_gap: Source files of example A (links 'added after upload')

gaps.map_says: six source-file folders (kick-off email, first OR and packing slip, Amazon build and OR revision, quote and dims, customs packet, BOL); the Amazon shipment and labels, the Freightcom quote and booking and tracking are still to come; Teams messages were not provided
